GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2017-08-25T12:21:01Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Copy some JSON element into a given JSON string
Description: Hi,

Running this code make the program eat all available memory. It's actually the call to the `cJSON_AddItemToObject` function that does it.

        cJSON *root = NULL;
        cJSON *params = NULL;
        cJSON *someparam = NULL;
        const char *jsonString =
                        "{  \"params\":"\
                        "  {"\
                        "    \"someparam\":"\
                        "    {"\
                        "      \"attribute\": \"value\""\
                        "    }"
                        "  }"\
                        "}";

        root = cJSON_Parse(jsonString);
        params = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "params");
        someparam = cJSON_GetObjectItem(params, "someparam");
        cJSON_AddItemToObject(params, "someparam", someparam);

        printf("cJSON_Parse root : %s\n", cJSON_Print(root));
        printf("cJSON_Parse params : %s\n", cJSON_Print(params));
        printf("cJSON_Parse someparam : %s\n", cJSON_Print(someparam));

Obviously, I'm doing something wrong here and I'd like to have your feedback on how to re-insert an existing JSON element into a given JSON string, safely.

Thanks!

You must provide a category number (1-3). Your response must follow this format exactly:

CATEGORY: [category number]
REASONING: [your reasoning here, including specific reasons why an issue would be hard to dockerize if choosing category 3]
llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue involves a memory leak problem in cJSON library usage. The problem is that the code is trying to add an item (someparam) to an object (params) when that item is already part of the object. This creates a circular reference that causes memory consumption to grow uncontrollably. 

This is a conceptual programming issue that can be analyzed without needing to build or run the code. The problem is clear from code inspection: when `cJSON_AddItemToObject(params, "someparam", someparam)` is called, it's trying to add an object to itself, creating a circular reference.

The solution would be to either:
1. Create a deep copy of the someparam object before adding it
2. Remove the item from params before adding it again
3. Use a different approach that doesn't involve re-adding the same object

This type of issue can be verified through code analysis without needing to compile or execute the code, as it's a fundamental programming logic issue related to how the cJSON library handles object references.
